title: Compact journey transitions and surface prioritization notes
content:
Purpose:
This doc captures a focused set of design notes for the console navigation redesign: specifically, how compact (collapsed) surfaces should transition between routes, how we prioritize surface real estate across task flows, and backlog items that unblock engineering implementation.

Problem statement / context:
- Console is growing vertically (more pages / per-model and per-route surfaces). The left rail in full mode works, but collapsed/compact mode feels brittle: users lose task context when routes change and deep links often land in unexpected subviews.
- We need consistent transition semantics so that compact users (small screens, power users who prefer minimal chrome) can move between Tasks -> Model -> Deploy -> Metrics without losing ephemeral task state (e.g., prompt drafts, evaluation token).
- Current fallback behavior (force-full-page load when route incompatible) is leading to friction and unexpected full-page jumps.

Design goals:
1) Preserve task context across route transitions where reasonable (keep drafts/unsaved state for TTL or until explicit discard).
2) Make compact-mode transitions predictable: predictable animation, clear affordance for when a surface will open in modal vs full route swap.
3) Minimize cognitive overhead: surface prioritization matrix that decides which UI primitives remain visible in compact mode (breadcrumbs, micro-actions, quick-search).
4) Provide canonical deep-link behavior so product links shared over Slack always land in a consistent state (canonicalized route + optional anchor params).

Key concepts / definitions (for alignment) :
- Compact journey: sequence of user actions while console chrome is in collapsed/compact mode (left rail collapsed, top header only).
- Surface: any interactive area (sidebar panel, right detail pane, modal, full page).
- Transition affordance: the visible cue that tells the user whether the next view will be an overlay or a route replacement.
- Route succession policy: deterministic rule that chooses where navigation lands given current surface/compact state (ex: open-in-panel if current model matches; otherwise route-swap with soft-preserve).
- Soft-preserve: keep ephemeral state in local storage/session cache for X minutes and restore if user returns to the same surface.

Proposed behavior (high level):
- Entry-mode heuristics:
  * If user arrives via deep-link with explicit anchor (eg ?pane=metrics&anchor=latency-chart), respect anchor and open target pane even in compact mode.
  * If user navigates from within console: evaluate route succession policy. If target is a sibling detail view of current model (same top-level entity), open as right detail pane overlay. Otherwise perform route swap and keep a soft-preserve snapshot of the previous pane.
- Transition animation: 150ms fade + slide for panel openings; 220ms slide-left for route swaps. Keep reduced-motion settings respected.
- Breadcrumb tokenization: reduce breadcrumb length by tokenizing entity names (truncate middle) and show full name on hover/tooltip for compact screens.
- Deep-link canonicalization: for sharing links, the canonical link should include top-level route + canonical pane if applicable (ex /models/ggml-1.3?pane=evals). If a non-canonical deep-link is used, redirect to canonical + show a banner: "You were redirected to canonical view."

Surface prioritization matrix (draft):
- Essentials (always visible in compact): global search, quick-create (+), notifications, user account menu.
- High priority (visible when space allows / collapsed with icons + tooltip): active route icon, model picker mini (current model short name), context breadcrumbs.
- Medium (hidden behind single chevron): active route quick-actions (start evaluation, scale pool).
- Low (moved to overflow): audit logs, raw metrics explorer link.

Wireframe / microflow descriptions (notes for engineering & design):
- Compact state wireframe A: left rail collapsed to icons. Clicking a model icon opens an ephemeral right-hand detail panel (overlay) with two tabs: Summary / Recent Runs. Overlay height is full with small header; can be pinned to convert to route-swap.
- Compact state wireframe B: quick-launch keyboard shortcut (Cmd+K) opens a compact command palette that can trigger direct route swaps while preserving soft-preserve snapshots.
- Pinning affordance: small pin button in overlay header that when clicked converts overlay -> route-swap and updates browser history (so back works).
- Failure / capacity fallback: if the requested pane depends on a heavy data call (ex metrics that require a Topk query), show a lightweight placeholder with an explicit "Open full metrics" CTA to avoid full-page jumps in compact mode.

Backlog grooming (prioritized):
1) Implement route succession policy engine (PC-423) — impact: high, effort: medium. Acceptance criteria: deterministic landing for 90% of navigation flows, unit tests for policy matrix.
2) Soft-preserve session cache (TTL 12 min) for ephemeral panes (prompt drafts, eval inputs) — impact: high, effort: small. Acceptance: drafts survive tab switch and brief route swap, cleared on explicit discard.
3) Compact overlay component and pinning behavior (+animation) — impact: medium, effort: medium. Figma file linked above.
4) Breadcrumb tokenization helper utility (truncate + tooltip) — impact: low, effort: small.
5) Deep-link canonicalizer service (server redirect + banner) — impact: medium, effort: medium. Requires routing infra changes.
6) Lightweight metrics placeholder for compact mode — impact: medium, effort: small.

Open questions / tradeoffs:
- TTL for soft-preserve: short TTL (5–10 min) keeps memory low but might frustrate users who switch contexts. We suggested 12 minutes as compromise; need SRE input for memory impact.
- Pinning semantics vs browser history: should pin always push a history entry? If so, frequent pin/unpin could create noisy back navigation. Possible solution: use replaceState for pin; only push on first transition.
- When is route-swap preferable to overlay? We propose a topology-based rule: overlay for sibling detail routes, route-swap for cross-topology transitions (e.g., from a model to an org billing page). Validate with analytics on common transitions.

Acceptance criteria (UX + PM):
- No regressions for full-rail users. Compact-mode users should be able to: resume a draft after switching to another route within TTL, pin a panel and get a stable URL, and share deep-links that land in canonical view.
- Reduced full-page jumps by 70% for users in compact mode for top 10 navigation paths measured in GA.

Implementation notes for engineering:
- Start with a thin route succession policy module in JS: small deterministic ruleset expressed as ordered predicates. Keep policy as data for experimentation (feature flag toggles).
- Soft-preserve storage: use sessionStorage for ephemeral field-level snapshots and a small LRU on the client keyed by canonical route + user id. Fallback to server-side saving only for pinned panels.
- Animation: use CSS transitions + prefers-reduced-motion checks. Keep durations adjustable via tokens.

Design next steps / owners:
- Marisol: finalize surface prioritization matrix and update Figma with compact overlay variants (by 2025-03-07).
- Liam: spike on route succession policy engine and a small prototype for dev review (PC-423) (by 2025-03-10).
- Aisha: run a quick hallway usability test with 6 engineers to validate pinning + soft-preserve mental model (by 2025-03-05).

Notes from grooming session (2025-02-28):
- Engineering (Noah) flagged memory cost for keeping drafts across many tabs; agreed to LRU + TTL strategy.
- Product (Marisol) to create a small experiment to route-swap only for cross-topology transitions for 25% of traffic.
- Design suggested a subtle chevron microcopy: "Open as panel (pin to make permanent)" to reduce confusion.

Quick todos / follow-ups:
- Update Linear ticket PC-423 with prototype link and acceptance criteria (Marisol).
- Add analytics hook for transition type: overlay vs route-swap vs redirect (Liam).
- Draft copy for canonical redirect banner (Aisha).

References / inspiration:
- Notion compact mode patterns, Figma community small panel libraries, Airbnb internal header collapse notes (private).

If anything here is unclear or someone wants a live whiteboard session, ping me (Marisol) and I’ll set up 30m review.
